artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Silver Rings" is a single by Matt Berry, released in 2025 as part of his eleventh studio album, Heard Noises. The track exemplifies Berry's eclectic musical style, blending elements of rock, funk/soul, and folk into a distinctive sound that is both accessible and intricately layered. With its smooth grooves, melodic hooks, and Berry's signature vocal delivery, "Silver Rings" reflects the album's broader exploration of genre fusion, anchored by his knack for crafting songs that feel both classic and contemporary.

As a standout moment on Heard Noises, "Silver Rings" marks a return to vocal-driven songwriting for Berry after his 2023 instrumental release, Simplicity. The song and the album as a whole have been praised for their inventive arrangements and genre-blurring approach, with critics highlighting the record as one of Berry's strongest to date. Released through Acid Jazz Records, "Silver Rings" and Heard Noises received widespread acclaim, with outlets such as Record Collector and Louder Than War lauding the album's creativity and musical depth, cementing its place as a highlight in Berry's diverse discography.
